release_focus: Shared-query mechanisms, loss-scale floors, certified threshold stability, matched-cohort capacity diagnostics, exact batch-precision completion for all 1,098 instances, decision-tolerance evaluation of unchanged policies, and a supplementary safe retrieval gate with warm, cold and archive-aware access accounting.
title: Adaptive Reading Budgets for Joint Forecast Audits with Cumulative Data
abstract:
Background. Model audits share verification readings across predictors. We ask when choosing later readings after earlier answers reduces the number needed for precise comparisons.

Methods. We combine sharp comparison intervals, adaptive query planning and exact randomized-batch certificates, with replay on cumulative meters.

Results. Under compact convex uncertainty, for one comparison, if a deterministic policy guarantees precision with two exact scalar readings, some randomized fixed batch succeeds with worst-case probability at least 1/2. This lower bound disappears with two comparisons. For every m>=3, we construct instances where adaptation always succeeds but the best randomized batch succeeds with worst-case probability exactly 1/m. All coordinates are queryable, the budget remains two, and each comparison is separately certifiable by a fixed batch. The separation also holds for all pairwise comparisons among three models. On 225 of 1,098 meter blocks across six systems, two adaptive readings guarantee joint half-width precision where three fixed readings are necessary. In 191 cases, every scalar comparison separately needs at most two fixed readings, isolating a shared-budget obstruction. We certify optimal randomized-batch precision on all 1,098 blocks. Optional-reading reductions are 6.40% and 7.67% across the panels. Absolute-precision and capacity analyses identify when simpler fixed plans suffice. Unrestricted bulk retrieval is faster on the tested public interface.

Conclusions. Sharing a budget can make feedback necessary even when separate comparisons need none. The meter study identifies when feedback saves readings and when simpler protocols suffice.
